slides.title: Section 1 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 1 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
1.4 Reflection: "Think of a goal your team set in the last 12 months. Was it an Objective, a Key Result, or a task disguised as one of these? What would a proper Key Result look like using the formula?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one real goal.
Say which of the three it was: an Objective, a Key Result, or a task.
Then rewrite it as a Key Result with all four elements: the verb of change, the metric, from X to Y, and the deadline."
Listen for: a rewritten Key Result with no baseline. Ask: "From what, to what?"

§4. Bridge to Section 2.
Say: "We have the toolkit. Section 2 asks why the sequence matters."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 1 of the participant file: 1.4 Reflection.

pictures.alt: Reflection 1.4: Think of a goal your team set in the last 12 months. Was it an Objective, a Key Result, or a task disguised as one of these? What would a proper Key Result look like using the formula?

slides.title: Section 2 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 2 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
2.2 Reflection: "At which point in the SiP → KISS → OKR sequence does your organisation typically enter? What is the consequence of skipping the KISS stage?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name the point of entry: Success in Practice, KISS or OKRs.
Give one piece of evidence from your organisation’s last planning cycle.
Then name one consequence you have seen when the KISS stage was skipped."
Listen for: a consequence stated as a feeling, such as “people were frustrated”. Ask: "What did it cost, slow down or leave undecided?"

§4. Bridge to Section 3.
Say: "We know the sequence and why it matters. Section 3 asks where it breaks down."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 2 of the participant file: 2.2 Reflection.

pictures.alt: Reflection 2.2: At which point in the SiP → KISS → OKR sequence does your organisation typically enter? What is the consequence of skipping the KISS stage?

slides.title: Section 3 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 3 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
3.1 Reflection: "Which hot zone description most accurately reflects how you instinctively approach OKR definition? What would you need to do differently to write an enterprise-level Key Result?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Start the thinking in the room.
Ask: "Which of these descriptions resonates most with how you instinctively write Key Results?"
Take two answers.

§4. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one hot zone description.
Give one objective or Key Result you have written that shows it.
Then say what you would do differently: which SiP domain you would add, and which role you would consult."

§5. Bridge to Section 4.
Say: "We know the filter, the building blocks, the steps and our own biases. Section 4 is where your group builds."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 3 of the participant file: 3.1 Reflection.

pictures.alt: Reflection 3.1: Which hot zone description most accurately reflects how you instinctively approach OKR definition? What would you need to do differently to write an enterprise-level Key Result?
